_law: RC-325, operator mandate 2026-08-09 (roughly the tenth instruction): ONE and only ONE producer for every field in this repository, Schwab leaf or derived. Many consumers are expected and correct. A consumer CARRIES the produced value; it never recomputes it.
_why_this_file_exists: Every prior faucet lock was scoped to the surface failing in front of me: single_faucet_provenance sees 3 kl_* keys, phase2a_level_lock governs 19 level ids, and server.py emits 592 distinct payload keys. Enforcement over a domain requires the domain to be enumerated. This file IS that enumeration, and tools/check_one_producer.py quantifies over it.

_verdicts.PASS: registered field, exactly one computing site, and it is the declared producer
_verdicts.FAIL: registered field computed in two or more sites, or in a site that is not the declared producer
_verdicts.NOT_PROVEN: field not yet registered. Counted and reported via `tools/check_one_producer.py --measure`, never silently passed. 2026-09-21 correction: the prior text here cited tests/test_one_producer_registry_v1.py, a file that does not exist and never asserted a shrinking count — no enforced check currently gates this remainder from growing; it is a reported number, not yet a locked one.

_payload_surfaces_note: RC-325/SP-05: the files whose emitted fields are classified as registered or NOT_PROVEN. Declaring them makes their ABSENCE a fail-closed violation — the checker raises PayloadSurfaceMissing rather than reporting zero unresolved fields, because 'I could not look' must never read as 'there is nothing there'. A fixture repo that declares none is silent by design; this repo declares server.py and therefore cannot pass while it is missing. RC-REHAB-1 (2026-09-23): the list now names server.py AND every module the server.py decomposition extracted from it (route modules, server_state_* phases, overlay/terrain/tier-A/gamma-surface/analytics-recompute modules). With server.py alone declared, each extracted slice silently removed its fields from this classification -- NOT_PROVEN read 310 on the branch against 668 on main, a shrink that was code moving, not fields being proven -- and the RC-292 naming gate stopped seeing _terrain_kl_overlay, the very writer it was built for. A module moved out of server.py that writes payload keys must be added here in the same commit.
_how_to_add_a_field: Name the field, the ONE module:function permitted to compute it, and the evidence you used to establish that it is the only one. Adding a field without deleting the competing sites is a FAIL, not a registration.
_naming_note: RC-292/2026-09-21: 'one producer' does not by itself prevent the SAME value being written to server.py's payload under a second, undocumented name (the kl_gsf/gsf duplication that motivated the fix). A field entry MAY add source_key (the literal string used to pull the value from the producer's own result/cache, e.g. the terrain-cache lookup key) and serialized_as (every payload key currently reviewed to carry that value). tools/check_field_naming_consistency.py enforces that every server.py assignment keyed off a registered source_key targets only a name in that field's serialized_as list — any other target key is reported as undocumented naming drift, not silently allowed.

gex_dollars_per_1pct_at_strike.evidence: RC-345 / F42 (NOT F14 — F14 is VWAP bands; ids F01-F40 immutable): the DISTINGUISHING signature of the dollar-GEX-per-1% quantity is the spot-squared scaling (the local `spt * spt` term). The prior generic inputs (gamma, openInterest, spot) false-matched math_probabilities.score_option_expression, whose only qualifying construct is `base += min(abs(gamma) * 10.0, 3.0)` — a scoring accumulation that mentions gamma but is NOT a $GEX derivation (no OI, no spot-squared: a legitimately DISTINCT semantic, and a local scalar never published as an exposure). Pinning computation_inputs to the actual producer variables (gamma, oi, spt) restricts the match to the one site that reprices gamma into dollars-per-1%: math_exposure_core.compute_exposures_by_strike (call_gex_1pct / put_gex_1pct at lines 288/315). Locked by tests/test_single_producer_batch_f02_f13_v1.py (the `* spt * spt * 0.01` arithmetic appears in exactly two lines, both inside that one function).

gamma_support_floor.formula: GSF = highest strike s < spot where N(s) <= phi * N(spot) on the repriced net-GEX profile N (the SAME materialized profile the gamma flip/regime use, RC-345 one-profile rule); phi = GSF_PHI = 0.5. Fail-closed to None (state=BELOW_SUPPORT) when N(spot) is already at/below eps = GSF_EPS_FRAC * max(|N|).
gamma_support_floor.evidence: 2026-09-21: repo-wide search (git-tracked, non-test/tool/research files) for compute_gamma_support_levels, and bare 'gsf'/'grc'/'gamma_support' tokens, found exactly two hits: math_levels.py (the producer, whose own docstring self-identifies 'RC-354: Gamma Support Floor (GSF) + Gamma Resistance Ceiling (GRC) -- ONE producer') and terrain_engine.py, which calls it once (line 764) and carries the result into its own dataclass fields (gsf/grc/gsf_state) -- a consumer carrying the value, not a second computation. GSF_PHI and GSF_EPS_FRAC, the function's own threshold constants, are each defined exactly once, immediately above the producer, ruling out a parallel implementation with different parameters. No AST pass was run (unlike the GEX$/1pct entry, which needed one to disambiguate a false match) because the plain-text search already came back with exactly one hit outside the declared producer, and that hit is a structural carry, not a competing derivation.

gamma_resistance_ceiling.formula: GRC = lowest strike s > spot where N(s) <= phi * N(spot) on the SAME repriced net-GEX profile GSF uses -- one function call returns both levels together, never computed separately. phi = GSF_PHI = 0.5, same fail-closed rule as GSF.
